title: Hom into a module is left exact, and Hom out of a finite free module is a finite product
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $N$ an $R$-module. (1) Let $M_1\xrightarrow{f}M_2\xrightarrow{g}M_3$ be $R$-linear maps with $g\circ f=0$, $\operatorname{Ker}g=\operatorname{Im}f$ and $g$ surjective. Write $g^*:\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_3,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_2,N)$, $\psi\mapsto\psi\circ g$, and $f^*:\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_2,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_1,N)$, $\chi\mapsto\chi\circ f$. Then $g^*$ is injective and $\operatorname{Ker}f^*=\operatorname{Im}g^*$; that is, $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_3,N)\xrightarrow{g^*}\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_2,N)\xrightarrow{f^*}\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_1,N)$ is exact. (2) For $n\ge0$ let $R^{\oplus n}$ be the free $R$-module with standard basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$. Then $\chi\mapsto(\chi(e_i))_{1\le i\le n}$ is an $R$-linear bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R^{\oplus n},N)\to N^{\oplus n}$, with inverse $(y_i)_i\mapsto\bigl(\sum_ir_ie_i\mapsto\sum_ir_iy_i\bigr)$.
